# Agent-doc sync contract

**The package is the source of truth; the SKU repo is the distribution; `--check` is the
enforcement.** The same three-part shape as codegen and `Scaffold.Sync` — no new concepts.

## Why a sync exists at all

A registry-resolved package lands in `Library/PackageCache/<name>@<version>/`. That path is
version-suffixed, `.gitignore`d, and — decisively — **not loaded into an agent's context by
anything**. An agent could read it if told the exact path, but nothing would be diff-reviewable and
no reviewer could see which rules were in force for a given commit.

Agent context loads from the **project root**: `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (plus their `@` imports)
and `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`. Nothing under `Packages/` or `Library/` qualifies. So the pack must
be materialized into the repo — and once it is materialized, it can go stale, which is what
`--check` is for.

## What lands where

| Source (`Documentation~/agent/`) | Destination in the SKU repo | Ownership |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | `docs/framework/README.md` | **generated** — overwritten every sync |
| `AGENTS.framework.md` | `docs/framework/AGENTS.framework.md` | **generated** |
| `architecture-map.md` | `docs/framework/architecture-map.md` | **generated** |
| `sync-contract.md` | `docs/framework/sync-contract.md` | **generated** |
| `framework-api.index.json` | `docs/framework/framework-api.index.json` | **generated** (and itself regenerated from the package sources) |
| `recipes/*.md` | `docs/framework/recipes/*.md` | **generated** |
| `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | **generated** |
| `tools/*` | `Tools/pf/*` | **generated**, and written with the execute bit |
| `agents-region.md` | a marked region inside the repo-root `AGENTS.md` | **region generated, the rest of the file is yours** |
| `SUBAGENTS.md` | `docs/framework/SUBAGENTS.md` | **generated** — the contract the SubagentStart hook injects; a SKU adds its own in a repo-root `SUBAGENTS.md`, which the sync never writes |
| `hooks/*` | `.claude/hooks/*` | **generated**, and written with the execute bit |
| `bmad/<skill>.pf.toml` | `_bmad/custom/<skill>.pf.toml` — only when `_bmad/` exists | **generated** — the framework's BMAD layer; the SKU's own `_bmad/custom/<skill>.toml` is never written |
| `gitignore.block` | a marked block inside the repo-root `.gitignore` | **block generated, the rest of the file is yours** |
| *(code: `HostSettings`)* | single keys in `.claude/settings.json`; in `.mcp.json` and `UserSettings/AI-Game-Developer-Config.json` only when they exist | **key owned, the rest of the file is yours** — each key is a minimum or a presence, spliced in place |

### Why the sync reaches past the three folders

The tools in `Tools/pf/` are written against a host tuned for them — a 15-minute Bash ceiling, an MCP
client that waits for a long Unity suite, a plugin that does not give up on the Editor after 10 s — and
the build skills are told how to use those tools by facts that live in BMAD's customization, not in a
skill this pack ships. Shipping the tools without that tuning and those facts is how every new SKU
re-discovered the same aborts and the same wasted turns. So the pack ships them together, under the same
three-part shape: the package is the source, the SKU repo is the distribution, `--check` is the
enforcement.

**The BMAD layer.** The BMAD fork merges a skill's customization as `customize.toml` (the skill's own)
< `_bmad/custom/<skill>.pf.toml` (this pack) < `_bmad/custom/<skill>.toml` (the SKU) <
`_bmad/custom/<skill>.user.toml` (a developer). The pack only ships APPEND-shaped keys there —
`persistent_facts`, keyed `thorough_lenses` — so a SKU's facts add to the framework's and a SKU lens
with the same `id` replaces the framework's. A scalar (`route_selection`, `implementation_handoff`) set
in this layer would silently mask every later fix the fork makes to it, so scalars belong in the fork's
base `customize.toml`, never here. Ownership inside `_bmad/custom/`: the fork's
`apply-story-sizing.sh` owns `bmad-create-epics-and-stories.toml`, this pack owns `*.pf.toml`, the SKU
owns everything else.

**The host keys.** A host file is never re-serialized: the sync splices the one key it owns at its
recorded span, so the bmad-loop hooks beside the framework's hook and the plugin token beside the
timeout never churn in a diff. A larger value a developer chose is kept. In the Editor, the sync door
and the Setup Wizard also raise the running Unity-MCP plugin's in-memory timeout through the plugin's
own setter — the plugin writes its config back on every settings change, and would otherwise revert
the file the sync just fixed.

`Tools/pf/` is to `Tools/` what `docs/framework/` is to `docs/`: a framework-owned subtree inside a
SKU-owned directory. A SKU's own `Tools/<anything-else>/` is never written to, so the tools land
beside the SKU data they read — `Tools/UiGate/probes/`, whose coordinates and token names belong to
that one game — without either side having to negotiate for the same folder.

## The four ownership rules

1. **A generated file is overwritten in full.** Each carries a header naming the framework version
   and the command that produces it. Editing one is pointless — the next sync reverts it, and
   `--check` is red until then. The header is written in the destination's own comment syntax and
   below anything that must stay on line 1: an HTML comment under a `SKILL.md`'s YAML frontmatter, a
   `#` comment under a tool's shebang (`#` is the one comment syntax `sh` and Python share, and a
   `#!` line is only honoured as line 1).
2. **The `AGENTS.md` region is bounded by markers.** Only the text between the `PF:AGENT-DOCS:BEGIN`
   and `PF:AGENT-DOCS:END` HTML comments is owned by the sync. Everything outside them is yours and
   is never touched. If the markers are absent, the sync appends the region at the end of the file;
   if `AGENTS.md` does not exist, it is created with the region as its only content. A begin marker
   with no matching end marker is a **corrupted region** and is an error (exit `2`) — appending a
   second region would leave two contradictory rule blocks in a file an agent reads every turn.
   Markers are matched **only at the start of a line**, so a document that quotes them in prose
   (this one does) still syncs correctly.
3. **Nothing outside the destinations above is written, and nothing is ever deleted.** The
   destinations are exactly `docs/framework/`, `.claude/skills/pf-*/`, `Tools/pf/`, `.claude/hooks/`
   (the pack's hooks only), `_bmad/custom/*.pf.toml`, the two marked regions (`AGENTS.md`,
   `.gitignore`), and the owned keys of the table above. The sync creates no scaffolding and touches no
   manifest. It also does **not** remove a file
   it once generated but no longer does — if a pack entry is renamed upstream, the old file lingers
   until you delete it. That is deliberate: a stale-removal pass is exactly how an earlier sync in
   this codebase silently stripped entries it did not own, and a leftover doc is a far cheaper failure
   than a deleted one.
4. **A tool lands runnable.** `Tools/pf/*` is written with the execute bit set, and the bit is
   re-applied on every sync — a tool that arrives on a checkout that dropped it is repaired without a
   content rewrite. On Windows there is no such bit: the files are written, `--check` never reports a
   permission difference it could not act on, and a tool is run through its interpreter
   (`sh Tools/pf/visual-judge.sh`, `python Tools/pf/pixel-probe.py`) or through Git Bash / WSL. A tool
   committed from a Unix machine still carries the bit in git's own `core.filemode` record, so the
   next Unix clone gets it back.

## The token budget this layout buys

| Tier | Content | Cost | When it loads |
|---|---|---|---|
| Always on | The `AGENTS.md` region + every skill's frontmatter `description` | ~1–2k tokens | Every turn |
| On demand | One `SKILL.md` body | ~0.7–1.5k tokens | When the task matches its description |
| Deep reference | `docs/framework/*.md`, the API index | as needed | When a skill or the agent points at it |

The whole pack read end to end is far larger than any always-on budget allows. That is the point:
the region makes an agent *aware* that all 17 rules exist, the skills carry the operational detail
for the task at hand, and the reference docs answer the questions the skills raise.

## `--check` semantics

`pf-build.sh agentdocs --check` (and `Framework/Doctor` check 10) compare, byte for byte, what the
sync **would** write against what is on disk:

| Exit | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Everything matches. | — |
| `1` | **Drift** — a generated file is missing, stale, or hand-edited; a `Tools/pf/` tool is present and byte-identical but not executable (`NOT+X`); or the `AGENTS.md` region differs. | Run the sync and commit the result. |
| `2` | **Error** — the package could not be located, or a source file is unreadable. | The message names the resolution attempts. |

Drift is expected and normal immediately after a framework version bump. That is exactly the signal
the gate exists to produce: the rules a SKU follows can never silently lag the framework code the
SKU actually resolved.

## Package resolution order

The sync locates the package by probing, in order:

1. An explicit `--package <path>`.
2. `<root>/Packages/com.classicspins.prototype-framework` — the embedded case, which is also how
   the framework repo syncs itself.
3. The `file:` dev-link path declared in `<root>/Packages/manifest.json`, resolved relative to
   `<root>/Packages/`.
4. `<root>/Library/PackageCache/com.classicspins.prototype-framework@*` — the registry/git case,
   newest match.

If all four fail, the error names each path it tried. A pinned consumer that has never opened the
project in Unity has no `PackageCache` entry yet — open the project once, then sync.
